criteria.criterion: The change description names the root cause: the driver enforces only a fixed wall-clock deadline and never tracks progress, so a stalled agent is indistinguishable from a slow one.
criteria.evidence: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased/Fixed: 'Root cause: the agent driver enforced only a fixed wall-clock deadline and never tracked progress, so a stalled agent was indistinguishable from a slow one.' The same statement is a comment at the stall check in claude.rs.

criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs runs a stand-in agent that emits nothing and hangs, with a long timeout. It asserts the driver ends it well before the deadline, with outcome TimedOut and a detail that says it stalled. It fails on the base commit and passes with the change. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.
criteria.evidence: a_stalled_agent_is_stopped_long_before_its_deadline passed: 'hang' stand-in, 12s timeout, asserts elapsed < 10s, TimedOut, and a detail containing 'stalled'. Fails on base, established by reading the code (checking out base would change git state): base procs.rs has no stall_window/stall_reason, so the test does not compile, and the base loop checks only the deadline, so the run would last about 12s with detail 'deadline of 12s reached'.

criteria.criterion: A test shows an agent that keeps emitting stream lines past the stall window is not killed early, and the existing deadline test (detail 'deadline of 2s reached') still passes. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.
criteria.evidence: an_agent_that_keeps_emitting_past_the_stall_window_is_not_stopped passed (7 lines one second apart against a 4s window, outcome Success). a_timed_out_invocation_is_timed_out_with_a_lower_bound (asserts 'deadline of 2s reached') passed; stall_window(2s) is None, so the deadline alone applies there.

criteria.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets, and cargo test --workspace all pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy passed, tests passed (1417 tests).

criteria.criterion: The stall rule is implemented once in the shared driver loop, not per role or per job, so every agent role gets it.
criteria.evidence: The only stall check is in ClaudeCodeDriver::invoke's receive loop (claude.rs, around lines 364-382), with the window derived from spec.timeout. There is no per-role or per-job code.

findings.summary: The stall window is shorter than the agent's configured Bash tool time limit, so a slow but healthy agent is killed as 'stalled'.
findings.evidence: Progress is only a new stream-json line. The agent writes no line while a tool call runs, and none during a long model turn either, because the driver does not pass --include-partial-messages (claude.rs:136). env.rs:79-86 gives the agent BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 and BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS=1200000 (athena.toml:61-62). With athena.toml's deadlines the silence allowed is: producer 3000s -> 1000s, verifier 2400s -> 800s (both under the 1200s Bash maximum), planner/critic 600s -> 200s and reader 300s -> 100s (under the 600s Bash default). One legitimate long command (for example a cold cargo test --workspace) is therefore cut off as TimedOut 'stalled'. That misjudges slow as stalled, the distinction the request asks for, and regresses healthy runs under the default configuration. No test covers a long silent tool call. Not measured on real jobs, because the job records are absent from this snapshot.

findings.summary: The 2-second floor is only meaningful for tests, yet the change description advertises it.
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG says 'after a third of its deadline (at least two seconds) of silence'. In production every deadline is at least 300s, so the floor never applies there.

findings.summary: The reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met
findings.evidence: The request asks to tell a stalled producer from a slow one. The reading takes progress to be 'any new stream-json line' and sets the window at 'about one third of the timeout', without allowing for the agent's own Bash tool limits (default 600s, maximum 1200s). Healthy agents can be silent that long, so this reading of progress cannot reliably tell stalled from slow.

request_reading_mismatch: The request asks to tell a stalled producer from a slow one. The reading takes progress to be 'any new stream-json line' and sets the window at 'about one third of the timeout', without allowing for the agent's own Bash tool limits (default 600s, maximum 1200s). Healthy agents can be silent that long, so this reading of progress cannot reliably tell stalled from slow.
summary: The change adds an early stop to the shared agent driver: if an agent's output stream stays silent for a third of its deadline, the driver ends it as timed out with the reason 'stalled', and the existing keep-the-partial-work path then applies. The root cause is named in CHANGELOG.md and in a driver comment. I ran cargo test -p athena-agent claude:: and all 12 tests passed, including the new stalled-agent and chatty-agent tests and the existing 2s deadline test. That the stalled test fails on the old code is established by reading it (no stall functions; the loop checks only the deadline), not by running it. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed (1417 tests). All five criteria are met. The verdict is fail because of one major finding: the window ignores the Bash tool limits the same driver gives the agent (600s by default, up to 1200s). The silence allowed is 1000s for a producer, 800s for a verifier, 200s for planner and critic, and 100s for a reader, so one legitimate long command can be killed as 'stalled'. That turns slow-but-healthy runs into timeouts, the opposite of the request's 'stalled versus slow'. Fix: keep the window above the Bash maximum plus a margin, or measure progress another way.
